item.name: Guides
item.description: Guides are static reference catalogs. They tell you which layer properties exist, which overrides a layer accepts, how to compose a template that looks good, and what the v2 editor document contains. They also tell you what a platform does to an image after you upload it, and what a given kind of image has to achieve. The content never changes between accounts, so you can cache a response and reuse it. These endpoints read no template and no company data. They also stay outside the usage log, so a guide call never appears there.

item.name: Editor documents
item.description: An editor document is the v2 draft of a template: its layers, its groups and every design-time property the editor shows. A template renders from that draft, so a change here changes what the next render draws. Every write is a compare-and-swap. Read the document, keep the `revision` it returns, and send that revision back. If the stored revision moved, the write returns `409` with the current revision and the current document. Rebuild the change on top of them and send the write again. Never resend the same body with the returned revision. `PATCH` applies a closed list of operations and changes only the properties you name. `PUT` replaces the whole document and drops every property you leave out. `GET /v1/guides/editor-document` carries the constraints both accept.

description.content:
Returns the stored v2 editor document and its revision. A template with no draft returns a null document and revision 0. Read this before every write.

Gates: throttle:editor-document.

Note: The read gate and the write gate name the same people. Every account in your company that can write the document can also read it.

item.name: Snaps
item.description: A snap renders a template (or every template in a collection) into a finished image or PDF, with your content substituted into each layer. Render synchronously for an instant result, or asynchronously with a webhook for bulk work.

description.content:
Renders a snap from a single template (`template_id`) or every template in a collection (`collection_id`). Provide exactly one of the two.

Synchronous (default): the response carries the finished `media_url` and returns 201.

Asynchronous (`async: true`): the snap is queued, the response returns 202 immediately, and the result is delivered to `webhook_url`. The webhook body is `{"event": ..., "snap": {...}}`. The event is `snap.completed` when the render succeeds, or `snap.failed` when it fails. A failed snap has `status: failed` and `last_error: render_failed`.

The API always renders the template's **published** version. Unpublished draft edits are not visible to the API until the template is published.

Gates: logApiRequest.

Note: Every response carries an `X-Request-Uuid` header. Quote it in support tickets.

Note: A collection request returns an array of snap objects, one per template.

Note: A response to a repeated `idempotency_key` carries an `X-Idempotent-Replay: true` header and renders nothing.

Note: `webhook_url` must be a public address. A host that resolves to a private, loopback, link-local or reserved range is rejected with 422.

Note: Each webhook carries three headers: `X-Snapsbrew-Delivery` (one ID for all attempts of a delivery), `X-Snapsbrew-Timestamp` (Unix seconds) and `X-Snapsbrew-Signature`. The signature is the HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of `{timestamp}.{raw body}` with the webhook signing secret of your company (**Account > Developers**). Compare it in constant time, and reject a timestamp that is more than five minutes old.

Note: An `idempotency_key` is honored for 24 hours. After that window a retry is a new request and renders a new snap.

item.name: Signed URLs
item.description: A signed URL renders a template from a plain `` or an `og:image` tag, with no API call and no bearer token. Your server builds the URL and signs it with a signed URL key from the Developers tab of the account page. The signing key is a secret. Sign only on a server. Never sign in a browser. The guide at /documentation/guides/signed-urls has code in PHP, JavaScript, Python and Ruby.

description.content:
Renders the published version of a template with the variants in the URL, then redirects to the image. A repeated URL redirects to the cached image.

To sign a URL:
1. Take every query parameter except `signature`.
2. Sort the parameters by key in byte order.
3. Join them as `key=value` with `&`. Use the raw values, not the URL-encoded values.
4. Compute the HMAC-SHA256 of that string with your signing key. Use the lowercase hex digest.
5. Add the digest as `signature`. URL-encode every value in the final URL.

Gates: signedUrlMiddleware.

Note: This route is on the site root, not under /api. The full URL is `https://app.example.com/signed-url/image.jpg`.

Note: The signed string holds every query parameter except `signature`, including a parameter that the server does not read. Do not send `identifier` or `api_log_uuid`, because the server reserves both names.

Note: A signed URL render counts in the usage log of the template owner.
(Required) UUID of the template. The signing key must belong to an active user of the company that owns the template.

The JSON array of Variant objects, encoded as standard base64 (RFC 4648 section 4, with `+`, `/` and `=` padding). Do not use base64url: the server decodes with PHP base64_decode. Sign the base64 value, then URL-encode it in the URL.
Image format. Defaults to png. Any other value renders png. The value is part of the signature. (This can only be one of png,jpeg,webp)
Set to 1 or true to render on a transparent background. Valid for png and webp. With format=jpeg it returns 400. The value is part of the signature. (This can only be one of 1,0,true,false)
(Required) Lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical string. See the description for the algorithm.

Generate images, PDFs and screenshots from reusable templates. The Snapsbrew API turns design templates into a render pipeline you can call from any stack.

Rate limits: every bearer endpoint is in the `api` group, which allows 60 requests per minute for one user (or one IP address when the request has no user). The two preview endpoints also allow 10 requests per minute for one user. The editor document endpoints also allow 30 requests per minute for one user and 180 for one company. Over a limit, the API returns 429 with a `Retry-After` header. Each response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`.
